impact_pathways.impact_narrative: IMP-4 (Tier 3 impacts.json) maps directly to EI-01. The fellowship delivers a jointly prepared Career Development Plan (D4-01, WP4) structured around the MSCA-PF mandatory training dimensions — digital and AI skills, open science, research integrity, knowledge valorisation, and innovation. The two-way transfer that is the defining mechanism of this project — the fellow's plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise into ELTE's geoinformatics group, and ELTE's remote-sensing and hyperspectral-fusion methods back to the fellow — creates a distinctive cross-disciplinary profile that broadens the fellow's career options in both precision agriculture and Earth observation. This project-specific exchange, documented in the CDP and enacted through WP4 supervision, directly realises EI-01.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: EI-02 requires that the fellow's communication and networking capacities are developed and deployed to broaden R&I impact. The project generates novel scientific and economic outputs across WP1–WP3 (diagnostic model D1-01, decision engine D2-01, validation dataset D3-01) that constitute substantive R&I content — specifically the end-to-end probabilistic fusion-to-WUE-decision pipeline — worth disseminating. WP5 (D5-01 Data Management Plan, D5-02 Dissemination and exploitation plan) formalises the open-science dissemination pathway under FAIR principles. WP4 (D4-01 CDP) develops the fellow's communication competences as a mandatory training dimension. Together these deliverables — grounded in IMP-1 (scientific advance), IMP-2 (economic/WUE impact) and IMP-4 (career/networking) from Tier 3 — constitute the project-specific mechanism through which EI-02 is realised.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: EI-03 targets the participating organisations' R&I capacity and knowledge transfer. The project contributes through two parallel mechanisms grounded in Tier 3. First, IMP-1 (scientific advance): WP1, WP2 and WP3 produce novel probabilistic sensing and decision-support outputs (D1-01, D2-01, D3-01) that directly increase ELTE's research output in remote sensing and precision agriculture, addressing the real-time decision-support gap identified in the vault (METH-SOTA-007). Both mechanisms are project-specific, traceable to named WP deliverables, and directly realise EI-03.

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: The project's primary outputs — scientific publications, the probabilistic fusion diagnostic model (D1-01), the decision engine and demonstrator software (D2-01), and the field validation dataset (D3-01) — are research artefacts intended for open dissemination under FAIR principles and permissive open-source licences. No patent protection is sought: the project operates at TRL 3–4 (RQ10 per impacts.json) and its impact is realised through open scientific dissemination and ELTE's research capacity rather than commercial exclusivity. This approach is consistent with the MSCA-PF instrument's emphasis on knowledge transfer and ERA capacity building (EI-03, EI-04).

sustainability_mechanism.description: Post-fellowship sustainability is secured through three complementary mechanisms grounded in the project's Tier 3 impact data. First, ELTE retains the probabilistic fusion methodology, validated code (D1-01, D2-01), and benchmark dataset (D3-01) as open research infrastructure within its geoinformatics and remote sensing group, enabling continued use and extension by ELTE researchers and students beyond the fellowship period (IMP-1, EI-03, EI-06). Second, open FAIR release of all primary code and data assets under the DMP (D5-01) ensures that the global precision agriculture and Earth observation research community can build on and extend the results independently, sustaining the scientific impact (IMP-1, IMP-2) without dependence on the project's continued funding. Third, the fellow's cross-disciplinary profile — coupling plant physiology and non-destructive stress phenotyping with geoinformatics and remote sensing, documented in the CDP (D4-01) — enables continued collaboration and career development in precision agriculture and Earth observation beyond the fellowship, sustaining the two-way knowledge transfer relationship between the fellow and ELTE (IMP-4, EI-01, EI-07).
